items.title: Sub-agency starts and sightings
items.requested: Starts or dated sightings across all 251 compiled sub-agencies, prioritizing 2002,2005,2010,2015,2020,2025.
items.finding: All 251 bodies were searched across 340 new service-plan/annual-report documents; 155 passages were manually reviewed. Deduplicated by body ID, 125 of the 158 originally undated records gain a start or accepted sighting: 111 queue sighting gains, 11 outside-queue sighting gains and three establishment-only gains, leaving 33. The 141 accepted sightings cover 134 bodies in total. The old importer accepts 144 touched queue records, including 111 previously undated records gaining a sighting, four earlier sightings and eight corroborating sightings. Five establishment claims are separate; three provide a date for records with no new sighting.
items.remaining_gap: 33 compiled records still have neither held nor newly accepted start/sighting in this F package. Some health records have separate health-package evidence; this branch total is not a combined deduplicated count. Machine candidates/nonmatches are not historical findings. Full six-checkpoint manual coverage and complete institutional lifecycles remain incomplete.

items.title: Sub-agency parents over time
items.requested: Replace inferred current-parent backfills, especially around the 2001,2005,2017,2020,2022,2024 reorganizations.
items.finding: 48 dated structural-parent observations and 42 separately typed administration/operation/funding/other relationships were recovered from charts and explicit organization descriptions. Major examples are 2002 Premier structures, 2006 Finance/Labour-Citizens’ Services/Forests charts and the 2024 Housing transition binder. Root separately supplies legal cabinet-transfer clauses.
items.remaining_gap: These are observations, not automatically continuous parent intervals. All 1,641 historical body-years have not been individually resolved and the baseline 1,609 inferred placements has not been recomputed after an atlas build. Older names and missing units require node identity work. Ministry budget/report cover alone is not structural placement.
items.integration_note: Use OIC 602/2020 rather than the superseded OIC 595/2020. Root transfer evidence is outside these F source/claim counts.

items.title: The sheriffs
items.requested: The administrative instrument combining nine offices in 1974; founding instruments for each county office from 1857.
items.finding: The complete 1974 and 1975 Attorney-General annual reports were retrieved through UBC’s official full-text API. The 1974 report dates planning to December 1973, expanded duties to 1 April 1974, the first training graduation to 5 July 1974, and staffing to nine sheriffs/246 deputies at 1 January 1975. The 1975 report shows continued implementation. These support a staged operational transition.
items.remaining_gap: No administrative nine-office amalgamation instrument was located. The complete county-office founding chronology from 1857 remains open. Nine justice regions are not the nine county sheriff offices. The 1976 Sheriffs Act is a later statutory recasting, not proof of the 1974 merger. API OCR has printed locators but was not independently checked against full scan images.

items.title: Enforcement and lands branches
items.requested: COS 1905 / 1961 / 1980 / 2002 instruments; Parks 1957 branch/1965 Act; Wildfire rename order; Surveyor General splits/2005/2019.
items.finding: Recovered original 1905 game amendment (assent 8 April), first warden report (organization/appointment 1 July 1905), 1961 terminology amendment (27 March), and 2002 statutory COS establishment (9 May). Recovered 1957 Recreation and Conservation Act (28 March) and 1965 Park Act (26 March). A wildfire plan records a 6 June 2015 terminology edit and July 2016 BC Wildfire Service sighting. LTSA’s official history supplies Surveyor General milestones 1851, 1858, 1873, January 2005 and 2019 at its stated precision.
items.remaining_gap: The 1980 COS administrative-branch instrument, 1957 Parks Branch creation instrument, Wildfire renaming order, and exact Surveyor General intermediate splits/2019 day remain missing. The 1957 department Act is not a Parks Branch establishment instrument; a plan’s terminology-edit date is not a rename order. The 1905 reporting-to-AG provision and 1906 report addressed to Provincial Secretary are kept as distinct facts.

items.title: Bodies that are gone, with a successor still drawn
items.requested: LCLB, EMBC, Industry Training Appeal Board, BC Ambulance Service, Provincial Game Commissioner, old Forest Service divisions, core-review tribunals.
items.finding: A 5 July 2018 official release expressly describes LCRB as formerly LCLB, establishing continuity and rename-by evidence. The 2001/02 report names nine safety committees/appeal bodies and the Small Business Forest Enterprise Program; older Forests charts identify vanished divisions and six regions. The later tribunal supplement resolves Industry Training Appeal Board continuation as Skilled Trades BC Appeal Board on 1 December 2022, preserving existing appointments.
items.remaining_gap: The exact LCLB rename day, EMBC legal endpoint/transition, complete Forest Service division lifecycles and all core-review tribunal endpoints remain open here. Old-name sightings do not prove abolition, and a proposed SBFEP transformation is not a completed event. Ambulance/health and other game-successor evidence must be integrated from the separate health/root packages.
items.integration_note: The 1 December 2022 continuation is in the tribunal supplement, not included in the 279 F claims. Eleven extra IDs have accepted sightings outside the 238-ID importer queue.

items.title: Environmental Appeal Board and Powertech date disputes
items.requested: EAB 1981 or 1982 commencement instrument; Powertech 1988 corporation versus 1989 service.
items.finding: OIC 2602/1981 commences the enabling sections, 2603 establishes EAB, and 2604 begins first appointments, all effective 1 January 1982 despite 18 December 1981 approval. Official registry credentials identify Powertech’s corporate predecessor incorporated 29 September 1988 and renamed POWERTECH LABS INC. 6 January 1989. BC Hydro describes a 1979 laboratory/service antecedent.
items.remaining_gap: EAB’s legal-start question is resolved. Powertech’s incorporation/name distinction is resolved; the exact operating launch is not established. Corporate identity, public name and laboratory function require separate events.

items.title: Logos, first-use evidence, artwork and permission
items.requested: Masters, first-use dates and permission for ICBC, BCLC, BC Ferries, BC Transit, WorkSafeBC; historical 1968/flag artwork; unknown/estimated dates.
items.finding: 36 sources/assets identified, 27 usable, 26 claims. Preserved seven authentic standalone artwork files and a 1986 printed BC Transit flag lockup. CIPO gives claimed use for ICBC insurance branding by March 1992, the ferry flag by 22 December 1983 and ferry waves by 1 July 2003. BCLC’s 2008/09 report documents a rebrand by 30 June 2009; filing/advertising events are kept separate. WorkSafeBC’s official history corroborates 1968/1983 design stages and 2005 name use. Published permission policies were collected.
items.remaining_gap: No original authoring master was verified and no atlas-specific reuse permission obtained. WorkSafeBC’s 1968 artwork and the BC Transit flag master remain unfound. Indexed Transit graphic standards/2008–09 report returned 404; Ferries FOI 23-016 historical-guideline release was indexed but returned maintenance/503. Registry filing, advertising and registration dates are not first-use dates.

G2.finding: All 35 current roster records reviewed;32 supported current Schedule applications,7 scoped to statutory officeholders. Three exact current limbs unresolved, with positive independent coverage/route evidence preserved. Extracted 614 named authority observations for 2019/20 and 2020/21, 370 distinct printed labels.
G2.remaining_gap: No first-coverage dates or automatic 2026 backfill. Exact current Schedule limbs for CRT, WCAT, Managed Forest Council remain unresolved. Historical authority-table labels can be retrospective; absence is not exclusion.

G3.finding: Current enabling provisions or official appointment records reviewed for 35 boards,tribunals,panels,branches and statutory offices. Mixed appointment/election routes and officeholder identities preserved.
G3.remaining_gap: Historical appointment-rule changes and full current name-by-name rosters are not complete. RTA specifies Public Service Act appointment but not the particular appointing official in the reviewed section.

G4.finding: 35 current served-population/subject-jurisdiction observations derived explicitly from enabling provisions, plus 14 explicit service-population/function claims in the F package.
G4.remaining_gap: This is not a full population map for all 251 sub-agencies or every historical period. Tribunal jurisdiction is not a managerial accountability line.
